facts.statement: The study used Xenopus laevis embryos to test how blocking the V-ATPase enzyme with the drug bafilomycin A1 affects the formation of the neural tube.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Genes and proteins involved in packaging ATP and glutamate into vesicles were found in the embryos between developmental stages 12.5 and 20.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Treating the embryos with the drug caused more incomplete neural tube closure at stage 20 and slowed the movement of specific cells in the dorsal neuroepithelial region.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: At stage 18, the drug lowered the levels of ATP and glutamate in the fluid surrounding the embryos while leaving the amounts inside the embryos unchanged.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Adding the NMDA receptor agonist partially fixed the incomplete closure caused by low and medium doses of the drug, but adding ATP did not have the same effect.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The results suggest that V-ATPase-dependent processes help build up extracellular ATP and glutamate for neural tube closure, but the study did not directly measure how vesicles load or release these molecules.
facts.subject: animals
